title: HF digital modes
blurb: Explain FSK, WSJT-X clock timing, FT8/FT4/FST4/Q65, mode traits, bandwidth versus speed and ALE.

E2E01.why: Data emissions below 30 MHz use **FSK**: shifting the carrier between set frequencies.

E2E02.why: WSJT-X stations agree on period boundaries by **synchronizing their computer clocks**. No sync pulse is sent.
E2E02.trap: There's no sync field or sync pulse in the signal.

E2E03.why: FT4's "4" is its **four-tone continuous-phase FSK**. Its cycles are 7.5 s, so eight per minute.
E2E03.trap: Four cycles per minute describes FT8, not FT4.

E2E04.why: FST4 has four-tone GFSK, **variable T/R periods** and seven tone spacings: **all of these**.

E2E05.why: WSPR is a one-way **beacon-style** mode, so it has no keyboard-to-keyboard chat. RTTY, PSK31 and MFSK16 do.

E2E06.why: An FT8 transmit/receive cycle is a fixed **15 seconds**, regardless of message length.
E2E06.trap: 8 is its tone count, not seconds.

E2E07.why: Q65 **averages multiple receive cycles**, which JT65 doesn't do.
E2E07.trap: Quadrature modulation and keyboard chat are not the difference.

E2E08.why: **PACTOR** is the one that can transfer binary files.
E2E08.trap: PSK31, RTTY and AMTOR carry text characters only.

E2E09.why: PSK31 uses **variable-length** codes: common letters get short bit patterns. RTTY's Baudot is fixed at five bits.

E2E10.why: **FT8** occupies about 50 Hz, narrower than the other three.
E2E10.trap: Don't confuse narrow bandwidth with speed: FT8 is slow.

E2E11.why: **Direct FSK** modulates the transmitter's VFO. Audio FSK instead feeds tones into an SSB transmitter.
E2E11.trap: Direct FSK isn't narrower or faster than audio FSK.

E2E12.why: ALE radios **constantly scan a list of frequencies** and activate when their call sign is received.

E2E13.why: **PACTOR IV** uses a wide channel and delivers the highest throughput in clear conditions.
E2E13.trap: FT8 trades speed for weak-signal sensitivity.
